subject: Pilot onboarding runbook and success criteria — ClearPath Labs
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ariane Lopez <ari.lopez@clearpathlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 30 Apr 2024 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot onboarding runbook and success criteria — ClearPath Labs

Thanks again for the time today, Ariane — good discussion. Below is a concise recap and a proposed runbook so we can lock the kickoff next week. Please reply with any clarifications or constraints.

Summary of customer pain / goals (what we heard):
- High variability in response latency on current vendor during peak traffic (P95 spikes to 1.2s).
- Cost per inference is unpredictable for bursty workloads; they want predictability for weekly batch jobs + real-time API.
- Need to keep PHI/PII in-house; cannot upload raw PII to third-party systems.
- Primary goal: reduce tail latency and unit cost for their QA assistant while ensuring no raw PII leaves their VPC.

Proposed pilot scope (4 weeks):
- Workloads: subset of customer QA queries (~10k tokens/day equivalent) + nightly batch of 50k records.
- Model profile: open LLM (quantized) + Redwood routing to a lower-cost variant for non-critical queries.
- Success metrics: P95 latency < 350ms for online queries, average inference cost <= $0.003/token equivalent for production mix, qualitative pass on 200-case prompt suite (>= 85% accuracy on intent-classification prompts).
- Eval plan: shared prompt set (see attachments) with blind scoring by ClearPath and Redwood.

Operational owners and roles:
- Customer: Ariane Lopez (ClearPath — Product/ops), Matt Chen (Infra — will provision VPC/S3).
- Redwood: Sergio Alvarez (Sales, owner), Laura Bennett (Customer Success — pilot ops), Neha Kapoor (Security & compliance lead).

Initial access and setup checklist (actionable items):
1) VPC peering or PrivateLink for model traffic — customer to open ticket with their cloud team (Matt).
2) Provide a sanitized sample dataset (S3 path or shared bucket) — "sample-qa-sprint.csv" (no raw PII).
3) IAM/service account with read-only access to the sample S3 path (details in access-template.yaml).
4) Allowlist egress IPs (we'll send the list after you confirm VPC approach).
5) Share a short backlog of 200 prompts for our eval harness (we can accept hashed prompts if needed).

Proposed timeline (target):
- Today (Apr 30): Agree on runbook and owners.
- May 1: ClearPath provides access approach + sanitized sample dataset.
- May 3: Redwood provisions pilot environment and shares egress IPs.
- May 6: Pilot kickoff call (30–45m) and environment validation.
- Weeks 1–3: Eval runs and weekly syncs.
- Week 4: Acceptance review and go/no-go decision.

Attachments: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (charter), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (owners/timeline), access-template.yaml (IAM sample).

Open questions for ClearPath:
- Can you confirm whether hashed/opaque prompt sets are sufficient for initial eval?
- Any internal approval needed for peering within the next 48 hours?

Next step: Ariane — please confirm owners and which access option (VPC peering vs PrivateLink) you prefer. If all good I’ll schedule the May 6 kickoff at 10:00 PT and send a calendar invite.

Thanks,
Sergio
Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sergio_alvarez@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

---
(attachment stubs: pilot-charter-v1.pdf (pdf), mutual-action-plan.xlsx (spreadsheet))

On Tue, Apr 30, 2024 at 17:05 Ariane Lopez <ari.lopez@clearpathlabs.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Sergio — this is a helpful distillation. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
>
> 1) We cannot move raw PHI or patient identifiers out of our VPC. Any sample must be pseudonymized or hashed. Is that compatible with your eval harness?
> 2) For peering: our infra prefers PrivateLink for outbound-control reasons, but there is a ~3 business day approval process. Is there a short-lived alternative (e.g., secure upload to a customer-owned S3 with strict ACLs) to unblock the first two days?
>
> Also tagging Matt (matt.chen@clearpathlabs.com) on the infra ask. We’re good to aim for May 6 kickoff but we’ll confirm after Matt confirms the peering timeline.
>
> Ariane
> Product Ops | ClearPath Labs
> ari.lopez@clearpathlabs.com
> (attachment: internal-security-policy.pdf referenced)

Ariane,

Thank you — hashed prompts are fine for the blind eval; we only need the clear text for QA review if you allow it later, otherwise hashes + labels work. For the immediate unblock we can accept a customer-owned S3 upload (pre-signed URLs) and Redwood will only access the sanitized file via the provided signed URLs. I'll coordinate with Neha on compliance controls.

— Sergio

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Ariane Lopez <ari.lopez@clearpathlabs.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 01 May 2024 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding runbook and success criteria — ClearPath Labs

Appreciate the recap. Operational notes from CS/ops perspective and what I’ll own for the pilot: 

Operational runbook (concise):
- If PrivateLink approval takes >48 hours: use pre-signed S3 URLs + a dedicated, short-lived service account. We will only access objects referenced by the signed URL and will log every GET.
- Provide one example tokenized row and one raw-but-hashed example so our eval team can sanity-check the prompt/label mapping.
- We'll run a dry-run of the eval harness once we have the sample; expect a validation report in 24 hours after we receive the files.
- Weekly sync cadence: 30m on Tuesdays (status, blockers, next actions).

Security & compliance (Neha): Neha — can you confirm the checklist we need before we accept signed URLs (I’ve attached access-template.yaml).

Kickoff timing: May 6 at 10:00 PT is fine pending access. I’ll create the calendar invite and include links to the pilot-runbook Drive folder.

Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
(attachment: access-template.yaml)

> On Apr 30, 2024, at 3:10 PM, Sergio Alvarez wrote:
> > [original message omitted for brevity]

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio_alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Ariane Lopez <ari.lopez@clearpathlabs.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, neha_kapoor@redwood.com, matt.chen@clearpathlabs.com
Date: Wed, 01 May 2024 11:58:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot onboarding runbook and success criteria — ClearPath Labs

Thanks all — quick confirmation and next steps.

- Ariane/Matt: pre-signed S3 URLs are an acceptable short-term approach. Please send the sample files (hashed where necessary) to the bucket listed in the Drive doc or share the signed URLs directly with sergio_alvarez@redwood.com.
- Neha: I’ll rely on your checklist for logging and audit configuration; if you need tweaks I can escalate.
- Laura: please go ahead and book May 6 10:00 PT for a 45m kickoff (I’ll be on the invite).

Final pilot acceptance criteria (for recording in HubSpot deal):
- Technical: P95 latency < 350ms for the online subset measured over 24h of production-like traffic.
- Cost: steady-state cost <= target in mutual-action-plan.xlsx (see attachment).
- Quality: blind eval on 200 prompts >= 85% fidelity to intent labels.

I’ll update the HubSpot deal with the runbook links and the schedule (deal id CPL-2024-042). If nothing else, we’ll plan to validate access May 3 and reconfirm kickoff May 6.

Cheers — Sergio

(attachments referenced: pilot-charter-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx)
thread_notes: This thread captures discovery follow-up, operational runbook, access options (PrivateLink vs signed S3), and a 4-week pilot with success metrics. All internal participants are within the allowed mailbox set.
